MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 22, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:01 p.m., on March 22, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on March 17, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  March 22, 2022
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill announced that the City Council gave instruction to the City’s Negotiator, but
no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

Mayor Bucknum announced that Item 21 is being moved up right after Item 15.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation by Orange County Board of Supervisors Donald P. Wagner

  Received presentation from Supervisor Don Wagner.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Bucknum

1.  Resolution of Support with the Orange County Board of Supervisors and Orange
  County Law Enforcement to Eliminate the Threat of Fentanyl in our Community

  Mayor Bucknum gave her report.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt Resolution
  22-05 to Join with the Orange County Board of Supervisors and the Orange County Law
  enforcement in Committing to Eliminate the Threat of Fentanyl to our Community.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None,
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Nancy Van Dusen, M.V.: She criticized the ValueRock Open House on March 9, and said it was a
waste of time since there was no research-based forum. She outlined her interaction with
ValueRock Representatives at the Open House and stated all the reasons she feels this project is not
right for Mission Viejo.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Commented on the brave citizens of the Ukraine. She stated that she still has
hope that Council Member’s Goodell and Kelly will run for re-election in 2022 for a two-year term
instead of extending their terms. She reminded the Council that both the Candidate Statements and

City Council Minutes  2  March 22, 2022
 the 2020 Election Results stated that the term of office were for two years. Questioned the City
Attorney on the terms of office.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: He addressed the terms of Council Member’s Goodell and Kelley and stated
that there was no legal document to allow for extension of council terms if cumulative voting could
not be implemented. Discussed that the voters were never informed that if Council Members were
elected for two years that they could still serve four-year terms. Questioned the City Attorney and
stated that those voters in Districts 2 and 4 will be disenfranchised from electing the Council
Members in 2022.

Anita Goldin, M.V.: Spoke on the Housing Element Report to meet the goals of the State.
Questioned the Council and Staff why ValueRock’s Garden Plaza is being considered if they were
not part of the Housing Element. She stated that Value Rock’s College Center was identified as a
housing site and thirdly the Commerce Center on the other side of Marguerite/La Paz intersection
is also part of the housing element. She voiced concerns over traffic if these projects are approved
and asked the Council to not re-zone the Garden Plaza.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Commented on rumors of kickbacks and lies of misinformation regarding
the Garden Plaza project. He stated that the rumors are out of control and are damaging the City.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Expressed disappointment in the Council to block forty percent of voters to
be able to vote in this year’s election. She believes this was crafted for a desired outcome to remain
in elected office without a vote from the public. She outlined different points of the process and
welcomes an investigation to determine if City Leaders abused the process, mislead the public and
misapplied the law.

Attorney Curley stated that the City adopted its General Law as of 1988. The City terms of office
have always been four years. When the City called the Election for Trish Kelley and Brian Goodell,
it was not limited for two years. What the ROV chose to print is the ROV’s choice. They were
referencing the lawsuit which was linked to rank choice or cumulative voting and was not linked to
our Municipal Code, to the City standards, nor to State Law. It was a very single spoke to a very
large wheel. He said if you want to blend it all into one thing, that is their prerogative, legally we
think that very wrong.

Attorney Curley explained the process of the Developer and responsibility of staff. He explained
the split between legislative process and adjudicative. Legislative is the making of laws which
includes zoning, general plan and high-level regulatory things. The project across the street can’t
go forward under current general plan and zoning. The City has still not received final plans on
this project. What the City can do at this point is critically evaluate the zoning they have requested.
If they don’t get the zoning approved, the net result is there is no project that conforms. He
reminded residents that the City Council at the last meeting instructed staff to put together the
process by which we advance the consideration of zoning for this project, which is Item 21 on
tonight’s Agenda. Lastly, he said that if the zoning is not adopted that site stays Office Professional.

City Council Minutes  3  March 22, 2022
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths , and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 8, 2022, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated February 25, 2022 in the Amount of $883,952.39

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 4, 2022 in the Amount of $841,620.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  FY 2021/22 Mid-Year Budget Review for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 22-01 Amending the Fiscal Year 2021/22 Budget for the
  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority.

6.  FY 2021/22 Mid-Year Budget Review for the Mission Viejo Housing Authority

  Adopted Housing Authority Resolution 22-01 Amending the Fiscal Year 2021/22 Budget
  for the Mission Viejo Housing Authority.

7.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter FY 2021-22

  Received and filed.

8.  General Plan Progress Report for 2021

  Received and filed.

9.  Software Licensing Renewal for the Animal Services Center

  Approved purchase order to HLP, Inc. in the amount of $35,216.80 for software licensing
  and support renewal for the Animal Services Center.

City Council Minutes  4  March 22, 2022
 10. Renewal of Network Monitoring and Automated Cyber Defense Solution

  Approved purchase order to Darktrace in amount not to exceed $35,557.50 for renewal of
  Enterprise Immune System and Antigena network monitoring and automated cyber defense
  solution.

11. Master Joint Use Agreement between the City of Mission Viejo and the Saddleback
  Valley Unified School District

  Approved the Master Joint Use Agreement (A22-10) between the City of Mission Viejo and
  the Saddleback Valley Unified School District.

12. Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract 2022-2023

  Approved the Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract (A22-11)
  for 2022-2023.

13. Lower Curtis Park - Water Quality Improvements (CIP 20245)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Earth Construction and
  Mining, Inc. (ECM) (A22-12) in an amount not to exceed $891,247.00; and (2) adopted
  Resolution 22-06 Amending the Fiscal Year 2021/2022 Budget for Costs Related to CIP
  20245.

14. Purchase of Two (2) BMW Model R 1250 GS-P Police Motorcycles

  Approved the Purchase of Two (2) 2021 BMW Model R 1250 GS-P Police Motorcycles in
  the Amount of $74,496.08 from Long Beach BMW Motorcycles.

OLD BUSINESS

15. Core Area Vision Plan Presentation of the Site Analysis, Field Reconnaissance and Site
  Plan Studies

  Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay gave the staff report and presentation.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Raised questions on the Sales Agreement with the Kinstler Trust. Stated
  that government has no business running a business.

  Wade Weiman, Palos Verdes: Stated that he is in favor of the Core Vision Plan but raised
  concerns regarding the traffic and parking with Chick-fil-A.

  Mark Puente, Ladera Ranch: Raised concerns on the impact Chick-fil-A will have on parking.

  By consensus the City Council received and filed the presentation for the Core Area Vision
  Plan Site Analysis, Field Reconnaissance and Site Plan Studies.

City Council Minutes  5  March 22, 2022
 CITY MANAGER REPORT (Item 21 was taken out of order)

21. Proposed ValueRock Realty Mixed Use Zoning Regulations

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Lynn Holmes, M.V.: Appreciated that there has been more transparency among the Council
  this evening. She stated that she appreciates the historical value of the architecture of Miners
  Village and suggested something similar to that. She voiced that the businesses need to be
  given a chance to survive.

  The following expressed opposition to mixed-use zoning at the Garden Plaza and encouraged
  the Council to vote against apartments at this sight: Yin Lu, M.V.; Neil Butterbaugh, M.V.;
  Nonny Bailey, M.V.; and Diane Fikert, M.V.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Accused the City Attorney of being a bully. Referenced the two bonds
  Council approved for the Core Area, one for nineteen million and a second for twenty-six
  million. She voiced concerns on the mixed-use apartments and stated it appears that the
  Council is in favor of mixed-use housing perhaps three stories instead of six. She stated she
  is concerned with the Council manipulating the public like they did regarding the district-
  based voting the last five years. She pointed out the Kosmont Report and the history of
  discussions among the Council on this report. Lastly, she asked that the Council state publicly
  “no zone change”.

  Mary Wathen, M.V.: Pointed out that she is glad there will be school traffic hours study
  regarding this project and agrees that the Garden Plaza needs a refresh.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, receive report and
  directed staff to submit, and complete the public hearing process for, the ValueRock Realty
  requested Mixed-Use Zoning District through the Planning and Transportation Commission
  and City Council, in advance of the development application, General Plan Amendment, and
  Environmental Impact Report by mid-May.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

16. Catalytic Converter Theft Ordinance

  City Attorney Bill Curley gave the staff report and Chief of Police Vuong presented a
  PowerPoint.
City Council Minutes  6  March 22, 2022
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  introduce Ordinance 22-344 Adding Section 11.25 to Title 11 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code Establishing Regulations Prohibiting the Unlawful Possession of Catalytic Converters
  in the City.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CITY MANAGER REPORT (Continued) (Item 20 was taken out of order)

20. Housing Element Update

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister gave the staff report.

  Council Member’s asked various questions of Director Lister.

  By consensus the City Council received and filed the report.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17. Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) Report

  Council Member Kelley deferred her report to the Council Meeting on April 12, 2022.

18. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Raths.

19. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Receive report from Council Member Goodell.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

City Council Minutes  7  March 22, 2022
 Council Member Goodell expressed that he was pleased that there was a change in tone today about
the Council’s position on the Garden Plaza Project. He reminded everyone that this is private
property and he strongly believes in private property rights. He stressed that the private property
owner has the right to bring their concerns and request to the City.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she attended a Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for Madrid
Chiropractic and stated it is great to see new businesses opening up in the City. Lastly, she reported
that the Character Word of the Month is Integrity.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths welcomed the season of Spring in our City. He pointed out the beautiful
banners along Marguerite and La Paz that the American Persian Community invested thousands
of dollars and went through the process with the City. The banners will remain up until the end of
the month.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs responded to one of the comments this evening regarding the “City to break
the seal of the community in Mission Viejo” he pointed out the report from HCD that it is the State
that is breaking the seal. Mayor Pro Tem stated it’s important to understand what happens when
you live in a one-party state and quoted from SB866 portends to lower the age of consent to twelve
years old to get a COVID vaccination without parental consent. He reported that SB871 requires
that all children up to the age of seventeen years old have to get a COVID vaccination in order to
attend daycare, public and private schools with no exemptions. SB920 authorizes the medical board
to inspect a doctor’s office and their records without the patients consent. He stated that this is a
violation of HIPAA laws. SB1464 forces law enforcement officials to enforce public health orders
even if they oppose or adopt a policy to oppose a public health order. SB1479 requires schools to
consider COVID testing and create testing plans long-term. SB1390 censors any social media
platform that puts dissenting information that contradicts the government narrative, any information
regarding medicine or vaccinations, information regarding elections and conspiracy theories.
SB1184 changes the California Medical Privacy Act to authorize a health care provider or service
plan to disclose your child’s medical information to a school link service coordinator without
parental consent. AB1797 makes changes to the California Immunization Record Data Act for
government agencies to have access to all vaccine records in addition to just students. AB1993
requires all employees including independent contractors to show proof of COVID vaccination to
work in the State of California. AB2098 classifies the Spring of COVID 19 Medical Opinion by
doctors and surgeon’s contrary to CDC narrative as misinformation and as unprofessional conduct
that will result in disciplinary action. He stressed that local government, school boards, water
boards, and police officers are losing control and its absolutely quackery what is going on and
having to do with censorship. He reminded residents that within fourteen months the City was able
to put back into our reserves the fourteen million dollars cash that we paid for the golf course.
Finally said that the Community Services Commission voted one way for the Core Area and the
Planning Commission voted another way

City Council Minutes  8  March 22, 2022
 Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum stated that elections matter and stressed that changes need to made in California
and that changes on this Council will not fix what is being placed on this Council by the State. She
wished that those that are vilifying this Council would focus their efforts a little further north in the
State. She announced that they are in the process of setting a date for the Sober Living Town Hall
Meeting which will be sometime the beginning of May. She thanked Council Raths for bringing
forth the ideas for Nowruz, which is a beautiful celebration of Spring within the Persian
Community. Mayor Bucknum attended the Terrace on the Green’s St. Patrick’s Day celebration.
Lastly, she thanked everyone for attending the meeting this evening.

ADJOURNMENT AT 9:58 P.M. TO TUESDAY, APRIL 12, 2022, AT 5:00 P.M.

______________________________________________
Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 12, 2022

City Council Minutes  9  March 22, 2022
